changes.new: Cash sales where the seller made the first contact, price $25 or more (32 M.R.S. 4661 to 4668); credit sales solicited and signed at the residence fall under 9-A M.R.S. 3-501 to 3-505 instead; both on top of the federal rule
changes.support: Cash sales: 32 M.R.S. 4661 to 4668, only where the seller made direct contact "without the consumer soliciting the initial contact", gross price $25 or more.

changes.new: Cash sales: within 3 full business days following the day the contract was made (32 M.R.S. 4664); credit sales: until midnight of the third business day after the day the buyer signs (9-A M.R.S. 3-502). Neither defines business day. Work stops only where the seller must affix merchandise permanently to the property.
changes.support: Title 32 says "within 3 full business days following the day on which the contract or sale was made"; Title 9-A says "until midnight of the third business day after the day on which the buyer signs". Neither section defines "business day".

changes.new: No state license for general contractors or trades such as roofing and framing; the State licenses plumbers and electricians
changes.support: In Maine, general contractors - and trades such as roofing and framing - are not licensed or regulated.
"Services" count as merchandise, so a cleaning sale started by the seller's visit or call is covered.

unsure: ME-ag: the addendum is required with every contract over $3,000 and should print, but the state file says it changes and must be re-fetched, so it is held rather than stored.

ME-ag: this one notice covers both the 1487(13) addendum and the 1487(14) website-and-phone notice; the second has no prescribed sentence, and the Attorney General's model contract section 14 links to a test host (uat) that must not be printed.
cancellation.no_work_or_payment_in_window left true: the file says work is barred only where merchandise is permanently affixed, which is a partial ban.

ME-1487, ME-1487-dispute, ME-1487-change-order: the statute's mandated sentences; the Attorney General's model differs in small ways (express warranties, check boxes with a fourth box, MUBEC). The statute's own words are the ones cut. applies now also requires residential (the chapter excludes buildings used for commercial or business purposes).

ME-cancel: now only the credit-sale statement (9-A 3-503), stored on file because the builder does not know whether a sale is credit. The cash-sale statements in 32 M.R.S. 4662(1)(F) and (G) have no prescribed wording and are not loaded.
